subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Checkout Aisle Psychology
description: A 60-second lesson on Checkout Aisle Psychology.

hook.text: Candy at the checkout counter generates $5.5 billion yearly in the US alone. You wait, you see, you grab.

buildup.text: Checkout aisles exploit impulse buying. After decision fatigue from shopping, your willpower is lowest at the register.

discovery.text: Items at checkout are small, cheap, and tempting. Low cost means no deliberation.

twist.text: Some retailers now offer healthy checkout aisles. Lidl replaced candy with fruit and saw no drop in revenue.

climax.text: At checkout, look away from the shelves. If it was not on your list before the queue, you do not need it now.

punchline.text: The checkout is the last persuasion attempt. Resist it.

quiz.question: Why are impulse items placed at checkout?
options: There is no other space in the store for them
Shoppers' willpower is lowest after decision fatigue from browsing
Checkout items have the highest profit margins
